spec.credit: UPSC CSE (Main) 2024 · General Studies Paper I · Q18
spec.text: Despite comprehensive policies for equity and social justice, underprivileged sections are not yet getting the full benefits of affirmative action envisaged by the Constitution. Comment.

scenes.vo: UPSC, twenty twenty-four. General Studies Paper One, fifteen marks, two hundred and fifty words. Policies for social justice exist, yet the underprivileged do not get the full benefit. Comment. Here's the strange part. The official numbers say both things are true.

spec.text: Despite comprehensive policies for equity and social justice, underprivileged sections are not yet getting the full benefits of affirmative action envisaged by the Constitution. Comment.

scenes.vo: Read what it asks. Comment means take a view, and back it. There are three jobs. Name the policies. Show why the benefit stalls. Then weigh it, with the Court's answer.

spec.title: Why Reservation Benefits Still Fall Short (UPSC GS I 2024)

lines.text: Articles fifteen and sixteen let the State make special provision.
Central posts carry fifteen, seven and a half, and twenty-seven per cent quotas.

scenes.vo: Start with the frame. Articles fifteen and sixteen let the State make special provision. Article forty-six is the directive. Central posts carry fifteen, seven and a half, and twenty-seven per cent quotas.

spec.title: Why Reservation Benefits Still Fall Short (UPSC GS I 2024)

lines.text: But in aggregate, the quotas are met.
Scheduled Castes and Tribes met fifteen and seven and a half per cent in twenty twenty-four.
In Group A, Scheduled Castes hold fourteen point two per cent.
Scheduled Tribes hold six point five four.

scenes.vo: But in aggregate, the quotas are met. Scheduled Castes and Tribes met fifteen and seven and a half per cent in twenty twenty-four. Look at rank, though. In Group A, Scheduled Castes hold fourteen point two per cent. Scheduled Tribes hold six point five four.

spec.title: Why Reservation Benefits Still Fall Short (UPSC GS I 2024)

lines.text: So the gap is about stock and spread, not only the total.
Backlog posts did not fall between twenty sixteen and twenty nineteen.
And the Court's judges differ on creamy layer for Scheduled Castes and Tribes.

scenes.vo: So the gap is about stock and spread, not only the total. Backlog posts did not fall between twenty sixteen and twenty nineteen. And the Court's judges differ on creamy layer for Scheduled Castes and Tribes.

spec.title: Why Reservation Benefits Still Fall Short (UPSC GS I 2024)

lines.text: But in twenty twenty-four, in Davinder Singh, seven judges answered part of this.
By six to one, States may sub-classify Scheduled Castes.
They need data showing inadequate representation.
The question's gap now has a legal test.

scenes.vo: But in twenty twenty-four, in Davinder Singh, seven judges answered part of this. By six to one, States may sub-classify Scheduled Castes. They need data showing inadequate representation. The question's gap now has a legal test.

blocks.text: The Constitution backs affirmative action through _Articles 15(4), 16(4)_ and 46, and posts carry quotas of 15, 7.5 and 27 per cent. Official records still show gaps.
1. Where the benefit stalls

• _Backlog_: unfilled reserved posts in ten Ministries did not fall between 2016 and 2019 (SC: 8,223 to 14,366); DoPT keeps no consolidated vacancy count. • Rank: in Group A, SC hold 14.20, ST 6.54 and OBC 19.14 per cent (1 Jan 2024), against the quotas (our comparison). • _Creamy layer_: OBC limit Rs 8 lakh since 2017; none for SC and ST in policy, and the judges differ. • Spread within groups: Punjab's 2006 Act gave half the SC quota first to two castes. • Education: ST gross enrolment is 22.8 against 30 overall (2023-24).
Bars: Group A shares against the quotas.
blocks.label: Fig. 1: Group A representation, 1 Jan 2024

blocks.text: 2. The Court's answer

• _Davinder Singh_ (2024, 6:1) allowed _sub-classification_ of SC, but only on data showing inadequate representation. • Article 335 is no bar. • Backlog drives have filled over 4.80 lakh posts since 2016. • The Rohini Commission, appointed in 2017 to study uneven OBC benefits, reported on 31 Jul 2023.
So the policy exists, but backlogs, uneven spread within groups and gaps in education show the benefit has not reached all. The way forward is data on representation, as the Court asked.

scenes.vo: Now we write. Two hundred and fifty words, about eleven minutes. Open with the Articles and the quotas. Then say that records still show gaps.

scenes.vo: Close with a balanced verdict. Policy exists and aggregate quotas are met. But stock, spread and access lag. The way forward is data. That is the view the question asks for.

weak.text: Reservation is given to all backward people, so everyone benefits.
weak.miss: the Court records that benefits are uneven within groups

weak.text: SC, ST and OBC are below their quota in government jobs.
weak.miss: aggregate SC and ST shares met 15 and 7.5 per cent at 1 Jan 2024; the gap is by rank

weak.text: The Supreme Court held that creamy layer applies to SC and ST.
weak.miss: the order is silent; judges differ
names no Article, case or report, so no evidence

scenes.vo: Now the easy answer beside it. It says all backward people benefit equally. The Court records that they do not. It says Scheduled Castes and Tribes are below quota overall. The gap is by rank. It says creamy layer applies to them. The order is silent, and judges differ. And it names no case.
